title: Your entry rules
desc: Write one entry rule you can see on the chart and follow every time

cards.title: Which rule can you follow?
cards.situation: You want a rule for when to buy. Which one could you follow the same way every time?

options.text: Buy when the stock feels strong
options.feedback: “Feels strong” changes with your mood. A rule must point to something you can see on the chart.

options.text: Buy when a rising stock pulls back to its rising 50-day average
options.feedback: You can check it on any chart, any day, and get the same answer.

options.text: Buy when people online say it’s going up
options.feedback: Online opinions change by the hour. A rule must point to something you can see on the chart.

cards.work: Test: give the rule to two people. Would both pick the same day? Only B passes.

cards.title: One setup, one sentence
cards.text: An **[[entry-rule|entry rule]]** says exactly what must happen before you buy. If you can’t say it in one sentence, it isn’t a rule yet.

rows.label: Confirm
rows.value: a day closes back above it

blocks.tip: Same rule every time. That’s what lets you measure it later.

cards.title: The rule on a chart
cards.text: One sentence: “Buy when a rising stock pulls back to its rising 50-day average and closes back above it.”

chart.label: A rising stock pulls back to its rising 50-day average near $47, then a day closes back above it: the entry

cards.foot: All three parts are there: the average is rising, price came back to it, and a day closed above it.

cards.title: Missed it? Let it go.
cards.text: Price bounced and ran far above the average. Buying now isn’t your setup. It’s chasing.

chart.label: The setup at the average near $44.60 was missed; price is now $52.60, 18% higher

blocks.tip: Buying up here also puts your stop far away. Same 1% risk, far fewer shares, and a worse price.

cards.rule: no setup, no trade. Another one always comes.

cards.title: Spot the real rule
cards.q: Which one is a clear entry rule you could test?

options.text: Buy good stocks when they’re cheap
options.feedback: “Good” and “cheap” mean different things to different people. Two traders would pick different days.

options.text: Buy when price closes above its 20-day high on twice its average volume
options.feedback: A close above the 20-day high and twice the average volume: both can be checked on any chart, so you can test it.

options.text: Buy when the trend looks up
options.feedback: “Looks up” is a feeling. A rule must name something you can measure on the chart.
“Buy the dips” doesn’t say which dip, how deep, or in what trend. B names exact things you can check.

cards.title: Wrong trend
cards.q: A stock is falling and its 50-day average points down. Price rises to touch the average. Does your pullback rule say buy?

options.feedback: A touch isn’t enough. Your rule starts with a rising average, and this one is falling. No setup, no trade.

options.text: No: your rule needs a rising average
options.feedback: Your rule starts with a rising average. This one points down, so there’s no setup and no trade.
A bigger position doesn’t fix a missing setup. The average is falling, so the rule says no trade.

options.text: Only if the news is good
options.feedback: News isn’t part of your rule. The average is falling, so the setup isn’t there.

cards.headline: You have an entry rule you can follow.
lines: A real rule fits in one sentence.
Trend, trigger, confirm: all three before you buy.
No setup, no trade. Don’t chase.
